episode.episode_title: AWS cloud capacity: what is really sold out?
episode.episode_description: AWS's biggest capacity allocations are largely booked into 2027, but CEO Andy Jassy says the company still reserves some on-demand EC2 and Bedrock supply. We explain why that distinction matters.
episode.selection_reason: Lead verified business story from today's Daily Brief; source previously blocked, now linked to a direct report.

selected_story.headline: AWS large capacity commitments stretch into 2028
selected_story.source_title: Amazon cloud capacity sold out through 2027, CEO Jassy says (23 October 2026)

short.title: AWS capacity: what's actually booked?
short.description: AWS has large commitments through 2027 and into 2028, but reserves on-demand EC2 and Bedrock capacity. Not all cloud computing is unavailable. https://suite.sapiverpress.co.uk/daily-brief/
short.script: Amazon's CEO says large blocks of AWS capacity for 2027 are mostly committed, with some of 2028 already reserved. But AWS still holds capacity for on-demand EC2 and Bedrock customers. That is an important difference from saying the entire cloud is sold out. Read Sapiver Forge's Daily Brief.
